title: Atlas master-reference knowledge contract
scope: Repository-owned, client-free reference model for the Atlas network-assessment and migration platform.

truth_contract.declared_scope_promise: Nothing in this versioned declared scope is left unclassified.
truth_contract.open_world_promise: Emerging, estate-specific, and not-yet-classified signals remain visible in a separate Open Horizon Register; no percentage claims completeness for the industry.
truth_contract.support_rule: Catalog inclusion means the topic is understood and classified, not that Atlas implements it. Only state=current is an end-to-end support claim, and every such claim cites a live owner.
truth_contract.partial_rule: State=partial names the implemented slice and links the remainder to an actionable gap.
truth_contract.training_rule: Labs, primers, and external-source summaries are advisory learning content only. They never become assessment evidence, alter the canonical snapshot, or establish vendor support.
truth_contract.client_data_rule: This layer contains no client, device, personal-vault, credential, or raw collection content.

controlled_states.meaning: Implemented for the explicitly bounded scope and grounded in a live owner.
A cited implementation exists, but breadth, depth, evidence stages, or surfaces remain incomplete.
The capability belongs in the declared catalog but no implementation is claimed.
Deliberately unavailable until a named human, evidence, safety, dependency, or authority gate clears.
Intentionally outside the product boundary; the exclusion and rationale are explicit.
The repository cannot currently establish implementation, applicability, or estate adoption.

Canonical assessment facts and reconciliation verdict.

Filesystem and bounded-input assertions.
Same-read custody, identity, digest, and mutation detection.
Protocol health, L1-L4 bounded path reasoning, operational findings, and scores.
Architecture-class detector catalog and observed/clean/finding/not-observed semantics.
Bounded expected-versus-abnormal state advice for selected protocols.
Opt-in, HTTPS, GET-after-login APIC and vManage collection.
Fourteen interactive Explorer modes and digital design-token owner.
Twelve-member deliverable family, ten CLI artifacts, and two web-only artifacts.
Per-run artifact inventory, chain, sealing, and receiver verification.
Built-archive inventory and clean-environment distribution verification.
Registry integrity, provenance, authority, and scoped-authority semantics.
Exact bounded lifecycle mapping and abstention.
AssessHub routes, intake limits, server-owned trust labels, and decision APIs.
Web summary and presentation mapping.
Independent redaction verification for supported outputs.
Repository and release privacy scanning.
Quarantined, sanitized external advisory-feed production.
HTTPS, SSRF, redirect, address, time, and byte controls for the research lane.

Static, local, repository-owned, non-operational master-reference boundary.
Cited, verified, client-generic engine lessons.
Release version and package entry points.

current_baseline.statement: Atlas is an automated senior-network-engineer platform for read-only L1-L4 brownfield assessment and migration governance.
The architecture registry currently declares 27 classes and 46 coverage-honest detectors across SSH and JSON evidence channels.
Protocol-health rows are currently produced for STP, EtherChannel, VTP, OSPF, BGP, EIGRP, and FHRP when their evidence is usable.
The offline Explorer registry currently owns fourteen interactive modes.
The deliverable family has twelve members: ten produced by a complete engine CLI run and two rendered only by AssessHub.
The master-reference site is static documentation: it accepts no evidence, stores no state, calls no runtime API, and is not another source of truth.

outcomes.title: Explainable current-state truth
outcomes.success_signal: A reader can traverse source evidence, custody, normalized fact, finding, decision, artifact, and proof without losing provenance.

outcomes.title: Coverage-honest assessment
outcomes.success_signal: Missing, malformed, conflicting, unsupported, and not-observed inputs remain distinguishable from healthy observations.

outcomes.title: Safer migration decisions
outcomes.success_signal: Recommendations remain separate from approval, execution, validation, rollback, and PIR evidence.

outcomes.title: One consistent delivery set
outcomes.success_signal: Executive, engineering, field, and machine-readable artifacts derive from the same canonical snapshot and identifiers.

outcomes.title: Portable, offline field use
outcomes.success_signal: Core assessment and verification work runs without external egress or ambient cloud dependencies.

outcomes.title: A targetable improvement map
outcomes.success_signal: Every incomplete capability links to a disposition, owner role, next action, and acceptance evidence.

outcomes.title: Controlled white-label reuse
outcomes.success_signal: Identity, terminology, theme, artifact furniture, and deployment policy change through owned contracts rather than scattered literals.

outcomes.title: Learning without contaminating truth
outcomes.success_signal: Internal lessons and external research can improve the product only through sanitization, provenance, evaluation, and explicit promotion.

outcomes.title: Business-value traceability
outcomes.success_signal: Technical findings connect to service impact, risk avoided, change effort, lifecycle cost, and acceptance outcomes without inventing financial precision.

maturity_model.label: Unclassified
maturity_model.exit_criteria: Scope, evidence, owner, and uncertainty are named.

maturity_model.label: Cataloged
maturity_model.exit_criteria: The capability has a stable ID, bounded definition, state, and gap disposition.

maturity_model.label: Observed
maturity_model.exit_criteria: Supported evidence can be collected or ingested with custody and coverage signals.

maturity_model.label: Assessed
maturity_model.exit_criteria: Deterministic parsing and analysis distinguish positive, negative, absent, malformed, and conflicting evidence.

maturity_model.label: Governed
maturity_model.exit_criteria: Findings drive traceable recommendations, human gates, artifacts, verification, and release evidence.

maturity_model.label: Measured learning
maturity_model.exit_criteria: Real outcomes calibrate the system through pre-registered, privacy-safe evaluation; no automatic policy mutation.

maturity_model.label: Autonomous closed loop
maturity_model.exit_criteria: Excluded by the current safety doctrine: Atlas does not write devices or self-approve changes.

current_maturity.basis: Bounded intake, same-read custody, canonical reconciliation, and manifest verification are implemented for supported shapes.
The engine has strong bounded campus and selected architecture detectors, while many enterprise, stateful, cloud, OT, and provider domains remain catalog gaps.
The governed workflow and twelve-member deliverable family have explicit owners and verification boundaries.
Atlas reasons over captured snapshots and selected logs; it does not claim a continuous metrics, flow, trace, packet, or synthetic telemetry platform.
Quality ledgers and evaluation contracts exist, but real-data calibration and vault-derived recall remain deliberately gated and coverage-honest.
Device writes and self-approved closed loops are non-goals.

non_goals.statement: No device configuration write, template push, remediation execution, or autonomous rollback.
No recommendation may approve itself or bypass human PR, peer-review, CAB, maintenance-window, and acceptance gates.
Repository sessions neither read nor write the personal vault; only a one-way sanitized digest may be consumed when separately produced on the owner machine.
The assessment engine and AST graph do not browse or call cloud models; connected research stays in a quarantined producer lane.
No catalog, score, test slice, or horizon watchlist may imply complete industry, estate, or repository proof beyond its denominator.
The master reference is not an operational console, evidence store, telemetry sink, analytics surface, or alternate source of truth.
Business-value views may expose inputs and ranges but never fabricate customer cost, revenue, probability, or risk-reduction figures.
A lab, protocol primer, vendor page, or external link never establishes current product support or a device-state fact.

lifecycle_stages.label: Discover
lifecycle_stages.question: Can the shape or domain be identified without invention?

lifecycle_stages.label: Collect
lifecycle_stages.question: Can evidence be acquired safely and with explicit authority?

lifecycle_stages.label: Bind custody
lifecycle_stages.question: Are the exact bytes and their identity bound to the run?

lifecycle_stages.label: Parse
lifecycle_stages.question: Are raw observations normalized deterministically and unknowns preserved?

lifecycle_stages.label: Analyze
lifecycle_stages.question: Can healthy, unhealthy, absent, malformed, and conflicting states be distinguished?

lifecycle_stages.label: Recommend
lifecycle_stages.question: Does the output explain evidence, consequence, action, caution, and uncertainty?

lifecycle_stages.label: Visualize
lifecycle_stages.question: Can a user explore the result without losing its evidence boundary?

lifecycle_stages.label: Deliver
lifecycle_stages.question: Do all relevant artifacts share identifiers, provenance, and completeness rules?

lifecycle_stages.label: Validate
lifecycle_stages.question: Does independent positive and negative proof cover the supported slice?

lifecycle_stages.label: Operate
lifecycle_stages.question: Are ownership, SLO, lifecycle, incident, and improvement signals defined?

planes.title: Evidence and custody plane
planes.purpose: Constrain intake, collect read-only evidence, bind identity and bytes, preserve raw observations, and surface coverage.

planes.title: Canonical truth and authority plane
planes.purpose: Normalize observations into one snapshot while preserving provenance, conflict, confidence, registry integrity, and source authority.

planes.title: Analysis and reasoning plane
planes.purpose: Compute bounded health, topology, blast radius, architecture conformance, protocol behavior, causal relationships, and abstentions.

planes.title: Decision and governance plane
planes.purpose: Keep recommendation, approval, execution, validation, rollback, acceptance, and PIR as distinct human-gated states.

planes.title: Experience and delivery plane
planes.purpose: Render the same truth for field operators, engineers, reviewers, executives, and machine consumers across offline and web surfaces.

planes.title: Assurance, release, and learning plane
planes.purpose: Verify privacy, determinism, archive contents, clean installation, quality trends, incident learning, and controlled knowledge promotion.

flow.contract: Only bounded, custody-bound observations enter canonical truth.
Reasoning consumes normalized facts and explicit uncertainty, never ambient memory.
Findings propose; they do not approve or execute.
Artifacts render gate state and provenance rather than replacing them.
The produced bytes, not only source intent, are verified.
Verified generic learning raises future controls without importing client evidence.

traffic_model.warning: These planes are investigative lenses, not OSI-layer replacements. A flow is only as complete as the evidence present in every traversed plane.

planes.title: Physical, optical, power, and timing
questions: Are links, members, transceivers, errors, power, and timing observed?
planes.current_scope: Interface, cable-map, neighbor, selected error, PoE, and platform evidence; no full optical/power/facilities model.

planes.title: Layer-2 forwarding and failure domains
questions: Which VLANs and links forward or block?
What partitions, reconverges, loops, or shares fate?
planes.current_scope: Strong bounded STP, VLAN, trunk, EtherChannel, shared-domain, blast-radius, and cable-map reasoning from captured evidence.

planes.title: Layer-3 underlay, routing, and gateway behavior
questions: How are prefixes, adjacencies, gateways, and failover paths selected?
Where are route or convergence uncertainties?
planes.current_scope: Selected IPv4/IPv6 routing, OSPF/BGP/EIGRP, FHRP, BFD, and topology reasoning; not a complete RIB/FIB or Internet-routing verifier.

planes.title: Overlay, tenant, and segmentation
questions: Which virtual networks and policy domains carry the flow?
Where can route leaking or shared fate cross a tenant boundary?
planes.current_scope: Selected VXLAN-EVPN, ACI, TrustSec, LISP, MPLS VPN, and SD-WAN evidence detectors; incomplete policy and tenant path proof.

planes.title: Stateful policy, identity, NAT, and service chaining
questions: Do forward and return sessions survive ACL, firewall, identity, NAT, proxy, and chain state?
Which policy decision and provenance allowed or denied the flow?
planes.current_scope: Explorer provides bounded ACL-oriented L4 simulation and the engine has selected firewall/identity detectors; no authoritative stateful session or NAT path engine.

planes.title: Application, service-delivery, and experience
questions: Do DNS, load balancing, proxy, TLS, application dependencies, and user experience succeed?
What latency, jitter, loss, MOS, and synthetic evidence exists?
planes.current_scope: Application-domain grouping is a visualization aid, not end-to-end application-delivery verification.

planes.title: Management, control, and observability
questions: Can control and management traffic reach authoritative services?
Are metrics, logs, flows, packets, traces, and time aligned?
planes.current_scope: Snapshot, selected controller, syslog, NTP, and protocol-state evidence exist; continuous telemetry and multi-signal correlation do not.

planes.title: External, Internet, hybrid, and cloud transit
questions: How does the service cross providers, clouds, SaaS, Internet, and organizational trust boundaries?
What are resilience, sovereignty, security, and egress-cost implications?
planes.current_scope: A bounded AWS security-group exposure detector exists; no complete multi-cloud, SaaS, Internet, or egress-economics path model.
